item.title: Gulf South food banks look back on a challenging year as another shutdown looms
item.description: Federal funding cuts and a 43-day government shutdown made 2025 a chaotic year for Gulf South food banks. For many, the challenges provide a road map for 2026.

item.description: The non-disclosure agreement was a major sticking point in a lively town hall that featured city officials, data center representatives and more than a hundred frustrated residents.

item.title: Immigration enforcement bill draws public backlash
item.description: President Trump has made immigration enforcement a centerpiece of his second term. A bill under consideration in the Alabama legislature would dovetail with those efforts by expanding what law enforcement could do on immigration in the state. We get more details about that and other legislative matters in our weekly check-in with Todd Stacy, host of Capital Journal on Alabama Public Television.

item.title: This Small Alabama Town Was Part of the Manhattan Project. Now It May Host a Hyperscale Data Center.
item.description: A town of less than 5,000 could be the site of a $6 billion data center project, its mayor says. Would the project be a boon or a burden?

item.title: Republican candidate challenges Tuberville residency, says he appears to live Florida, not Alabama
item.description: Ken McFeeters, who is running against Tuberville for the Republican nomination for governor, filed the challenge Tuesday with the Alabama Republican Party. McFeeters said he believes Tuberville lives in a multimillion-dollar beach home in Florida instead of a smaller home that he has listed as his residence in Auburn, Alabama.

item.title: Alabama inmate activists from an Oscar-nominated film are moved to solitary, attorneys say
item.description: Family members of the three men said they fear for their loved ones' safety and are concerned the moves to solitary confinement are a form of retaliation for outspokenness about problems within the prison system.
